newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi confirms 12,500T Iraq sugar sale.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi confirms 12,500T Iraq sugar sale.

text.p: Japan's Mitsubishi Corp confirmed on Wednesday that it has sold 12,500 tonnes of Thai white sugar to Iraq for prompt shipment under the oil-for-food deal reached with the United Nations last year.
But the company declined to disclose the selling price.
"We sold white sugar to Iraq, and further sales will depend on the Iraqi side's intentions," a Mitsubishi official said.
Thai sugar traders said earlier in Bangkok that the Mitsubishi deal was done well below the $390 a tonne offered recently to Iraq by a Turkish sugar firm.
The offer from the Turkish company was turned down not just because of the price level, but also as the firm intended to export the commodity by truck to Iraq, Japanese traders said.
Even before the U.N. deals were concluded, Iraq was buying sugar in the international black market, the traders added.
"The U.N. deal just enabled Iraq to buy openly, and we estimate they have already bought up to 150,000 tonnes of sugar so far," a sugar trader at a major Tokyo trade house said.
